subject: Brazil
note: Hand-curated research for a Geographica episode about Brazil’s neighbours. Claims are cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary). The article counts France as a neighbour through French Guiana; the count of ten is the sum of its list. France is not highlighted, so the Lawa headwaters flag is not touched.

claims.text: Brazil occupies nearly half of the land area of South America (47.7%).
Brazil borders all other countries and territories on the continent except Ecuador and Chile.

Brazil borders Uruguay to the south; Argentina and Paraguay to the southwest; Bolivia and Peru to the west; Colombia to the northwest; and Venezuela, Guyana, Suriname, and France (French Guiana) to the north.
claims.note: That is ten neighbours, counting France.
